Triple Red 7s Multiplier's prizes make it a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of the prize money still unclaimed, nearly all is in wins under $1,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

If "Triple Red 7s Multiplier" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
802.headline: What type of game it is

803.body:
Triple Red 777s's prizes make it a game with most of its money in small, frequent prizes. Of the prize money still unclaimed, about three-quarters is in wins under $5,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

Everything here about "Triple Red 777s" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through October 24.
803.headline: How prizes are split

804.body:
The top prize count on "Diamond Bingo" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has five of seven top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

Every line of Diamond Bingo's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
804.headline: Tickets sell, top prizes remain

805.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Multiply Your Money", about half are still unsold. The game is about halfway through its run, with four of seven top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Everything here about "Multiply Your Money" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through October 24.
805.headline: How far along this game is

806.body:
The most common win left on "Win $50, $100 or $200" is $50. The second biggest prize left is $100, and 55,868 of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

The table below shows the full count for "Win $50, $100 or $200", with every prize level included.

807.headline: Someone claimed a $20,000 prize

808.body:

The numbers for "Ravens X10" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.

"In the Green" is down to five top prizes after a $50,000 winner was claimed last week. The game started with seven top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

Everything above about "In the Green" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
810.headline: The top prize list got shorter

The numbers for "Extreme Green" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
811.headline: How far along this game is

812.body:

Every line of Loose Change®'s prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
812.headline: A top prize was just claimed

813.body:
"The Price is Right™" is in the middle of its run, with about two-thirds of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

Tomorrow's count on "The Price is Right™" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
